artists.biography:
Crowded House are a pop rock band formed in Melbourne, Australia in 1985 by lead-vocalist and primary songwriter, New Zealand-born Neil Finn. Other members have included his brother Tim Finn, Australians Paul Hester, Nick Seymour and Peter Jones and Americans Mark Hart and Matt Sherrod.
Crowded House has won several national and international awards. In Australia, the group has won eleven ARIA Awards from 26 nominations, including the inaugural Best New Talent award in 1987. The majority of their ARIAs were awarded for their first two albums, Crowded House and Temple of Low Men. They won eight APRA Awards from eleven nominations and were nominated for The New Zealand Silver Scroll for "Don't Stop Now" in 2007.
"Don't Dream It's Over" was named the seventh best Australian song of all time in 2001.

perplexity.description:
Crowded House’s eighth studio album, Gravity Stairs, was released on May 31, 2024, via BMG. The album blends rock and pop with a reflective, introspective tone, showcasing the band’s signature harmonies and melodic craftsmanship. Frontman Neil Finn leads the group—comprising Nick Seymour, Mitchell Froom, and Finn’s sons Elroy and Liam—through a collection of songs that grapple with themes of mortality, connection, and the passage of time. Tracks like “Magic Piano” and “Life’s Imitation” highlight the band’s adventurous spirit and emotional depth, while singles such as “Oh Hi” and “Teenage Summer” offer accessible, radio-friendly moments that recall their classic sound.

Gravity Stairs marks a significant chapter in Crowded House’s nearly four-decade career, demonstrating their continued creative vitality. The album stands out for its personal lyrics and nuanced arrangements, with songs like “Some Greater Plan (For Claire)” and “Night Song” drawing on intimate family history and real-world recordings. Critics have praised the record for its maturity and inventiveness, noting that the band avoids resting on past successes and instead delivers some of their most resonant work to date. The album was well-received for its thoughtful songwriting and enduring pop sensibility, reinforcing Crowded House’s reputation as one of rock’s most enduring and adaptable acts.
